extracted.intended_audience: early-career university-based scientists and engineers at invited institutions; research administrators and nominators
extracted.subtask_description: Program-level guidelines and selection priorities for the David and Lucile Packard Foundation’s Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering, describing who is eligible, how many fellows are chosen, award size/duration, and the program's emphasis on flexible, high-risk research. Intended for prospective nominees, nominators, and institutional administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target population — early‑career scientists and engineers
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is aimed at "the nation’s most promising early-career scientists and engineers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection focuses on early-career researchers showing exceptional promise; the Fellowship's purpose is to allow these individuals flexible funding to take risks and explore new frontiers in their fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional eligibility — invited institutions only
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, the Foundation "selects 20 Fellows from 50 invited institutions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The candidate pool is limited to individuals affiliated with those invited institutions (procedural eligibility constraint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection size and cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation selects 20 Fellows each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual cohort size is fixed at 20 Fellows; this affects competitiveness and nomination strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows receive individual grants of "$875,000, distributed over five years."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are sizable, multi‑year, and awarded per individual (not per project or institution), influencing planning and scope of proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows "can use their funds in whatever way would best advance their research."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship emphasizes flexibility—funds are intended to enable non‑traditional, exploratory, or high‑risk activities rather than being tightly prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on risk‑taking and bold ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are "encouraged to think big and look at complex issues with a fresh perspective."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates and proposals that propose ambitious, innovative, or high‑risk/high‑reward research directions rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: University‑based research strengthening
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is "rooted in David Packard’s commitment to strengthening university-based science and engineering programs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference and rationale center on supporting university research environments; nominees are expected to be engaged in university laboratories or academic settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of significant long‑term impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows have gone on to "receive the highest accolades, including Nobel Prizes... and elections to the National Academies of Science, Engineering, and Medicine."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit selection criterion: candidates should demonstrate potential to produce enduring, high‑impact contributions to their fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual (not institutional) awardee focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation awards "individual grants" to Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to individuals rather than to projects or institutions, indicating evaluation centers on the person’s trajectory and potential as much as on a single project.
